mkp-diagrams:er@1.about: An entity–relationship diagram: entities as cards of their attributes and keys, in columns by their relationships, joined row to row with crow's feet; picking an attribute or an entity lights its relationships.

inputs.name: entities
inputs.about: tables and their columns; kind marks primary and foreign keys (pkfk: both)

inputs.name: rels
inputs.about: a's side is left, b's side is right; acol and bcol name the attribute the line meets on each side (by default the foreign key, when the entity has one, and the primary key on the other side)

inputs.name: title
inputs.about: the header's title

inputs.name: caption
inputs.about: a line under the header; by default how many entities and relationships there are

inputs.name: lit
inputs.about: what starts lit: an entity, or entity.attribute

value.expr: filter(rels, r => indexof(names, r.a) >= 0 and indexof(names, r.b) >= 0)

values.name: tag

values.name: many
values.body: c == "many" or c == "zero_many"

values.name: keyed
values.body: map(filter(byname[nm].attrs, c => "" + c.kind == k or "" + c.kind == "pkfk"), c => c.name)

values.name: fromb
values.body: if(many("" + r.right) != many("" + r.left), many("" + r.right), not (len(keyed(r.a, "fk")) > 0 and len(keyed(r.b, "fk")) == 0))
comment: the side that holds the foreign key: the many side, else the one with a foreign key, else b

values.name: col
values.body: if(given != "", nm + "." + given, if(len(keyed(nm, k)) == 1, nm + "." + keyed(nm, k)[0], nm))
comment: where a line meets an entity: the attribute named, else its only key of that kind, else its title

value.expr: map(entities, e => {id: e.name, title: e.name, aside: "", external: false, rows: map(e.attrs, c => {id: c.name, label: c.name, badges: if("" + c.kind == "pkfk", ["PK", "FK"], if("" + c.kind == "plain", [], [tag("" + c.kind)])), meta: c.type})})

values.name: end
values.body: if(many(c), many, one)

**customers**: PK id `uuid`, email `text`, country `char(2)`

**orders**: PK id `uuid`, FK customer_id `uuid`, placed_at `timestamptz`

**order_items**: PK, FK order_id `uuid`, PK, FK product_id `uuid`, qty `int`

**products**: PK id `uuid`, name `text`, price `numeric`

- customers places orders, `1:0..*`
- orders contains order_items, `1:1..*`
- products appears in order_items, `1:0..*`
